newsitem.title: BOSNIA: Hardline Serb military chief Mladic dismissed.
newsitem.headline: Hardline Serb military chief Mladic dismissed.

text.p: Bosnian Serb President Biljana Plavsic has dismissed the Serb military chief, General Ratko Mladic, because of what she called "the well-known stand of the international community," the Bosnian Serb news agency SRNA reported on Saturday.
It said Plavsic announced that Mladic had been replaced by Major-General Pera Colic as part of a reorganisation of the Serb military command.

The agency, quoting from a presidential statement, said the army's General Command Headquarters had been renamed the "General Headquarters" and a number of other officers had been replaced in line with a parliamentary decision made in September.

"I regret that because of the well-known stand of the international community, I cannot name General Ratko Mladic the Chief of the Army Headquarters, so I would like to thank him and all the other members of the army headquarters, in the name of people of Bosnian Serb Republic, for all they have done for Serb people during the four-year war," Plavsic's statement said.
The Dayton peace accord which ended the war barred Mladic, who has been indicted for alleged war crimes, from any role in military or public life.

Despite the accord, the general remained in charge of the Bosnian Serb military machine, although he virtualy disappeared from public view after Dayton was signed last November, making only rare appearances at public military events.

The move to sideline Mladic came after a month of intense speculation in local media that he was about to be forced into retirement in an internal battle over the Bosnian Serbs' relationship to their Moslem and Croat counterparts.
It also ends a long-running dispute with the Bosnian Serb political leaders allied to the former president Radovan Karadzic.
Karadzic and Mladic publicly fell out early in 1995 when Karadzic failed in a bid to dismiss the general over allegations of treason and war profiteering.
